claims: Palm Sunday is a Christian holiday.
Palm Sunday commemorates Jesus Christ's triumphal entry into Jerusalem.
Palm Sunday marks the beginning of Holy Week.
Palm Sunday is celebrated on the Sunday before Easter.
Palm Sunday recalls cheering crowds laying palm branches in Jesus' path as he rode a donkey.
Palm Sunday marks the start of the final week of Lent.
According to the Gospels, Jesus entered Jerusalem just days before his crucifixion.
According to the Gospels, Jesus entered Jerusalem fulfilling prophecy.
The name Palm Sunday comes from the palm branches placed in Jesus' path as he arrived.
The palm branches placed in Jesus' path as he arrived were a gesture of victory and welcome.
Palm Sunday services begin with joyful "Hosanna" praises.
Palm Sunday services quickly move to a remembrance of the upcoming crucifixion (Passion).
Jesus rode a donkey instead of a war horse.
Catholic, Anglican, and Protestant churches hold special processions.
Catholic, Anglican, and Protestant churches hold blessings of palms.
